correctness.rationale: Write n_i=1+y_i, y_i≥0, sum y_i=r; for fixed k and N=k+r, HHI numerator=k+2r+Q(y), Q=∑y_i², while Shannon entropy E=log N−(1/N)log W(y), W=∏(1+y_i)^(1+y_i). Zero excess coordinates do not alter either Q or W, so integer partitions of r cover every fixed k with at least the nonzero excess count. Independent exact-int enumeration of all partitions for 0≤r≤7 gives strict reversal counts [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1], and tie splits first occur at r=6. At r=7 the unique pair is (3,4) versus (1,1,5); values Q=25<27 and W=800000>746496. Padding zero excess to any k≥3 proves the universal first-layer sharpness; for k=2 both indices are monotone in the larger share, so no reversal ever. This uses no floating logarithms.
residual_risks: This is an integer-grid same-k same-total theorem; neither real shares nor changing k are covered.
Finite enumeration is exhaustive for r≤7 but no claim is made about uniqueness of reversals at larger r.

value.rationale: A sharp resolution threshold for disagreement between two widely used concentration indices is a natural exact finite invariant for same-size fixed-firm market profiles, not a purpose-built arbitrary slice. The theorem identifies a universal first strict reversal across every k≥3, proves no reversal through six excess units, distinguishes a penultimate tie layer and proves uniqueness at the first layer, making the fact suitable for rigorous index-comparison applications.
residual_risks: Economic rankings are mathematical comparisons only; no antitrust, welfare, or policy inference.
